record.paper_title: Five open problems in theory of quantum information
record.original_question: Determine whether bound entangled states with negative partial transpose exist. In self-contained terms: decide whether there are bipartite quantum states that are entangled but nondistillable, while the partial transpose of the density matrix has at least one strictly negative eigenvalue; an equivalent Werner-state formulation asks whether there exists a negative-partial-transpose Werner state that is nondistillable for local dimension d>2.

evidence.quote: Problem 4: Establish whether there exist bound entangled states with negative partial transpose.

A quantum state is said to havepositive partial transpose (PPT)ifalleigenvaluesofitspartialtransposearenonegative. Otherwise, if some eigenvalues of ρΓ are strictly smaller than zero, the state has negative partial transpose (NPT).

However, in higher dimensional systems some entangled states can be distilled to a singlet form [127], but there exist also nondistillable entangled states, which are called bound entangled[128, 129].
This theorem implies that the current, fourth problem canbeformulatedasfollows: Decide, whether there exists an NPT Werner state which is nondistillable.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $\mathcal{H}_A = \mathcal{H}_B = \mathbb{C}^d$ with $d\geq 3$, and consider bipartite quantum states, i.e. density operators $ho$ on $\mathcal{H}_A\otimes\mathcal{H}_B$ (positive semidefinite, trace one). The partial transpose of $ho$ with respect to $B$ is the operator $ho^{\Gamma}$ defined by $(|iangle\langle k|\otimes |jangle\langle l|)^{\Gamma}=|iangle\langle k|\otimes |langle\langle j|$ extended by linearity. The state $ho$ is said to have negative partial transpose (NPT) if $ho^{\Gamma}$ has at least one strictly negative eigenvalue, and positive partial transpose (PPT) otherwise. A state $ho$ is separable if it is a convex combination of product states $\sigma_A\otimes\sigma_B$, and entangled otherwise.

A bipartite state $ho$ is said to be distillable if there exist an integer $n\geq 1$, a number $K\geq 2$, and local operations with classical communication (LOCC), i.e. a trace-non-increasing completely positive map of the form $\Lambda(\cdot)=\sum_i (A_i\otimes B_i)(\cdot)(A_i\otimes B_i)^{\dagger}$ on $n$ copies, such that the output $\Lambda(ho^{\otimes n})/\mathrm{Tr}\,\Lambda(ho^{\otimes n})$ has fidelity strictly greater than $1/K$ with the maximally entangled state $|\Phi_K^+angle=	frac{1}{\sqrt{K}}\sum_{i=1}^{K}|iiangle$ on $\mathbb{C}^K\otimes\mathbb{C}^K$. A state that is entangled but not distillable is called bound entangled.

For $d\geq 2$ and $p\in[-1,1]$, the Werner state on $\mathbb{C}^d\otimes\mathbb{C}^d$ is
$$W_{d,p} \;=\;  rac{1}{d^2-dp} igl(\mathbb{1} - p\,\mathbb{F} igr),$$
where $\mathbb{F}=\sum_{i,j}|ijangle\langle ji|$ is the swap operator. The state $W_{d,p}$ is NPT if and only if $p>1/d$.

Problem. Decide whether there exists a bipartite quantum state $ho$ on $\mathbb{C}^d\otimes\mathbb{C}^d$ for some $d\geq 3$ that is simultaneously NPT and nondistillable. Equivalently, decide whether there exist $d\geq 3$ and $p\in(1/d,1]$ such that the Werner state $W_{d,p}$ is nondistillable.
artifact.status_search_result: The existence of NPT bound entangled states (equivalently, nondistillable NPT Werner states in dimension d≥3) remains a long-standing open problem in quantum information theory. Recent works from 2024–2025 (e.g., new partial-trace inequalities for distillability of Werner states and reductions of N-undistillability to repeated 1-undistillability checks) report partial progress but do not resolve the question. Sources state the problem has been open for nearly 30 years.

status_evidence.title: Unveiling NPT bound problem: From Distillability Sets to Inequalities and Multivariable Insights
status_evidence.snippet: One of the oldest problems in quantum information theory is to study if there exists a state with negative partial transpose which is undistillable; this problem has been open for almost 30 years.
status_evidence.claim: The NPT bound entanglement problem remains open as of 2024.

status_evidence.title: New partial trace inequalities and distillability of Werner states
status_evidence.snippet: A new strategy translates the distillability condition on Werner states into partial trace inequalities, obtaining a new bound for 2-distillability of Werner states.
status_evidence.claim: Recent (2025) work provides only partial progress on Werner-state distillability.

status_evidence.title: Proving the distillability problem of two-copy 4×4 Werner states for monomial matrices
status_evidence.snippet: The distillability conjecture of two-copy 4×4 Werner states is one of the main open problems in quantum information.
status_evidence.claim: The Werner-state formulation of the problem is acknowledged as still open.
